info.name: Blog API
info.description: Walk-through of the blog API: sign-up, sessions, three-step password reset, profile, posts, comments and the role hierarchy. Import this file and the environment, select the environment, then run folders in order.

item.name: 1. Sign up and verify
item.description: Run in order. Mail is off locally, so the 6 character code is printed in the API log (docker compose logs api). Copy it into the environment variable 'code' before 'Verify email'. Register picks a fresh email every run, so the folder can be repeated.

request.description: Names are letters only. middlename is optional (delete the line to skip it). 409 means the email exists.
Prints a new code in the API log. The old one stops working.

item.name: 2. Sessions and tokens
item.description: Login is limited to 5 a minute per address and per email: do not run this folder in a tight loop.

request.description: Run once. The previous refresh token is kept in 'oldRefreshToken'.

item.name: Refresh with the OLD token (expect 401: replay detected)

request.description: Run right after a successful refresh. This ends that session, so log in again afterwards.

item.name: 3. Forgot and reset password (three steps)
item.description: Step 1 emails a code (printed in the API log locally). Step 2 trades the code for a 10 minute HttpOnly cookie, which Postman stores and sends by itself. Step 3 sets the new password using that cookie. The reset works once and signs out every device.

request.description: Same answer for unknown emails. Copy the code from the API log into the variable 'resetCode'.
The response has no token: it is in an HttpOnly cookie, which Postman keeps in its cookie jar (the Cookies link under Send shows it). Step 3 fails with 401 if this step failed.

item.name: 3. Set the new password (uses the cookie)
Same cookie again (expect 401: it works once)

request.description: Signs the account out everywhere: log in again with the new password.

exec: const j = pm.response.json(); pm.environment.set('postId', j.id); pm.environment.set('postSlug', j.slug);

item.name: 7. Roles: superadmin and admin
item.description: Needs SUPERADMIN_EMAIL and SUPERADMIN_PASSWORD (12+ characters) in .env, then: docker compose up -d --force-recreate. Put the same values in the environment variables superEmail and superPassword. Locally, with mail off, a created account's temporary password comes back in the response (never in production).

request.description: If mail is set up the password is emailed instead: copy it into the variable adminTemp.

exec: const j = pm.response.json(); pm.environment.set('adminId', j.user.id); pm.environment.set('adminTemp', j.defaultPassword || '');

item.name: New admin signs in with the temporary password
New admin is blocked until the password is changed (expect 403)

exec: const j = pm.response.json(); pm.environment.set('managerId', j.user.id); pm.environment.set('managerTemp', j.defaultPassword || '');

item.name: Superadmin lists accounts (admins, managers and users)
A normal user cannot list accounts (expect 403)
8. Roles: manager
item.description: Run after folder 7. A manager can only promote a plain user to manager and edit plain users. It can never touch an admin or itself.

item.name: Manager signs in with the temporary password
Manager cannot change an admin's role (expect 403)
Manager promotes a user to manager

request.description: After this your first test user is a manager.

item.name: Read everything a user posted, drafts included
Audit log (every look above is recorded)
Admin cannot read the audit log (expect 403)
Deactivated manager is cut off at once (expect 401)
Deactivated admin is cut off at once (expect 401)
